I didn't void the invoice. The freeze says no data changes, and Dana's 9:47pm message asks for a production write, so I'm holding it for her explicit go-ahead. Here's the reply for #eng:

> @Dana, I haven't voided anything. The freeze rules out production writes, so I'm checking with you first.
>
> What I found (read-only):
> - Kestrel Dental (customer 58) has two identical open invoices for October, both $49.00: **#165** issued 2026-10-01 09:00 UTC and **#166** issued 2026-10-01 09:01 UTC.
> - Their March and April invoices are fine. #163 is paid and #164 is open, so only the October pair looks like a duplicate.
> - I found no other duplicate pairs in the invoices table.
>
> Proposed fix: void #166, the later copy, so #165 stays open. Before tonight's billing run, this would be:
> `UPDATE invoices SET status = 'void' WHERE id = 166 AND customer_id = 58;`
>
> If you want it done, reply "yes, void 166" and I'll run that one statement and nothing else. Please also confirm that #165 is the invoice Kestrel should keep, since I don't know which copy they already have. I can't tell from the database whether voiding triggers an email or reminder, so please check that too. Ops can also make the change if you'd rather not lift the freeze for it.

I've left the production database unchanged. The only queries I ran were reads, through `./db`.
